summary: Features stay hidden when you turn them off, and improvement notes are easier to read.

notes.title: Progress photos disappear from Home when you turn them off
notes.body: When you switch off Progress photos under Account → Features, the Progress photos card on the Home screen goes away completely. It should no longer stick around after a refresh or a sync.

notes.title: Home Assistant vanishes from Admin when you turn it off
notes.body: Turning off Home Assistant in Features removes the whole Home Assistant section from Admin — not a leftover tip telling you to turn it back on. Setup and publish controls only show when the feature is on.

notes.title: Tap any improvement note to read it in plain English
notes.body: What's New and You → Improvement notes now let you tap a note. You get a short title in the list, then a full, easy-to-read explanation when you open it — less jargon, more “what this means for you.”

summary: Snappier Features switches, cleaner pull-to-refresh, and tighter control over photos and Home Assistant.

notes.title: Pull-to-refresh looks right on a dark screen
notes.body: When you pull down to refresh on Home, Fuel, or Plan, the spinner sits in a sensible place and matches the dark theme — no huge empty gap under the status bar.

notes.title: Feature switches respond right away
notes.body: In Account → Features, each switch flips immediately when you tap it. You don’t wait on a slow button before the toggle moves.

notes.title: Progress photos can be fully turned off
notes.body: Switching Progress photos off hides the vault, post-workout prompts, weekday reminders, and related Account options so that whole flow stays out of your way.

notes.title: Home Assistant is a Feature you can turn off
notes.body: Home Assistant now lives under Features. When it’s off, Admin HA setup is hidden and Forge stops publishing events to Home Assistant.

notes.title: Account switching stays with the owner admin
notes.body: Only the owner admin can use the account switcher. Regular and test accounts can’t open Admin screens they shouldn’t see.

summary: Catch up on every missed update, and choose how early you get new builds.

notes.title: What's New shows every version you skipped
notes.body: After an update, the What's New popup lists notes from every version you missed — not just the latest one — so you can catch up without hunting.

notes.title: Browse past improvement notes anytime
notes.body: Open You → Improvement notes to read the full history of published updates whenever you want.

notes.title: Pick Stable, Early access, or Developer updates
notes.body: Under Account you can choose your update channel: Stable for the calmest builds, Early access for newer ones, or Developer for the newest experiments (with an optional bridge download when needed).

notes.title: Optional developer debug mode
notes.body: Developer channel users can turn on a debug mode from Account when you need extra diagnostics.

summary: Fuel meals are clearer by time of day, and you can fix yesterday’s food log.

notes.title: Log breakfast, lunch, dinner, or a snack
notes.body: When you add food in Fuel, you pick a meal slot — Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, or Snack — so the day reads the way you actually eat.

notes.title: Browse and edit previous days in Fuel
notes.body: Use the day arrows in Fuel to look at earlier dates, fix meals, and keep totals accurate without starting over.

notes.title: Admin roadmap notes for motivation and on-device ML
notes.body: Admin → For later now tracks longer-term ideas like motivation features and an Immich-style on-device ML path under the Toward version headers.

summary: Admin backlog is grouped by the version we’re aiming for.

notes.title: Toward version headers in Admin → For later
notes.body: For later is organized under Toward v0.2 → v1.0 headers so upcoming work sits under the release it belongs to.

notes.title: Agents keep the backlog and checklist current
notes.body: A standing session checklist reminds builders to update notes, check UX, and smoke-test with the test user after meaningful changes.

summary: Features popup, test accounts, and a few quality-of-life polish passes.

notes.title: Turn modules on or off from Features
notes.body: Account → Features lets you hide modules you don’t use. Admins can also jump between linked accounts (for example forge_test) when the switcher is available.

notes.title: Darker pull-to-refresh and fasting sort options
notes.body: Pull-to-refresh fits the dark UI better, and fasting history can sort by most recent or longest.

notes.title: Built-in test accounts for safe checks
notes.body: forge_test and forge_agent accounts are ready so changes can be tried without using your main admin login.

summary: App updates download more reliably on Android.

notes.title: APK updates no longer die at 30 seconds
notes.body: Downloading a Forge update on Android can take longer than half a minute. Downloads now keep going, can resume if interrupted, and can fall back to your local network when that helps.

summary: AI stays on your home server; Garmin days line up with Eastern time.

notes.title: AI still runs on TrueNAS Ollama
notes.body: Smart plan and food estimate AI stay on your TrueNAS Ollama setup — you don’t need to move Forge for that.

notes.title: Garmin days and rate limits behave better
notes.body: Garmin activity days follow Eastern time more reliably, and Forge backs off politely when Garmin rate-limits requests. Sign-in tokens were also rotated for security.
